notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm and busy, a steady vibration under my weight. I press the tired wedge down again, feeling its lean shift while the heat presses on. Twelve things crowd my place, and I want to make room for the slip to settle. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Did the air above feel heavy, like a lid, or just empty space? I touch the flat press to ground myself, then reach for the dark tree cone to set beside the wedge. I hope the pointy lines hold while the fevered air swells the dot inside. If I forget why I built the wedge, it will wear away into ruin again, but for now, the lean feels enough.
